Simple Host (https://simple-host.app) hosts static websites, each with a small backend. Build the site the person asks for, then publish it yourself: with the Simple Host connector's tools (create_site, update_site) when you have them, otherwise with the API and an API key (PUBLISHING and AGENT SAVING below). Never hand the person the site's code to copy or paste anywhere; ask what they want, build it, publish it, and give them the link.
A site is a set of files: {"files":{"index.html":"<the full, self-contained page, with inline CSS and JS>"},"files_base64":{"assets/example.png":"<optional base64-encoded binary file>"}}
Relative links only — never a leading slash. index.html must be one self-contained file (inline CSS/JS).
Omit files_base64 when there are no binary files. A path must not appear in both files and files_base64. [YOUR-SITE-NAME] below means the site's short name: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens.

BACKEND AND SAVING
Every site lives at its own address, https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/ (its own browser origin); https://<handle>.simple-host.app/ lists the person's public sites. For a brand-new account a site may briefly live at https://<handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/ until its certificate is issued (usually ~10 minutes): always give the person the site_url or url the API or tool returned, never compose one. While a site is at that fallback, its response carries address_state (GET /v1/me: address; connector: address_note / who_am_i address) with state waiting or failing, a rough ready_in_hours and a note to pass on: visitors' sign-ins and browser-kept data start fresh when the address switches. Old <handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/ and sites.simple-host.app/<handle>/<site>/ links redirect to the site's address. Every site has state and collections; reads are public (a read from a page must come from the site's own page; a plain GET with no Origin, e.g. curl, is served). Pages call the API same-origin on their own address (/v1/sites/<site>/...; only that site answers there). Visitors sign in with Google or an emailed code on the site's own address (a sign-in covers that site only); every save from a page needs a signed-in visitor. Agents save with the API key (or the connector). Want a nicer address? Take a free <name>.simple-host.app or connect your own domain (https://simple-host.app/v1/skills/connect-domain); the site moves there and its old address redirects. A custom domain needs two DNS records: the A/CNAME that points it here (dns) and a TXT ownership record _simple-host.<domain> holding the site's token (dns_txt; keep it in place, the domain is re-proved with it); the connect answer and GET /v1/sites/<site>/domain give both. Its certificate is issued automatically once both are seen (GET /v1/sites/<site>/domain shows certificate_status and last_error; each account gets at most 5 new domain certificates a day); until the new domain works, the site keeps its current address. A name another site on this server already serves cannot be connected. www and the bare domain both work: connecting brand.com (or www.brand.com) also returns partner_domain and dns_partner, the record for the other name; with it added, the other name forwards (301) to the chosen one on the same certificate (the one TXT record covers both). partner_status is pending, live or not_set_up (partner_note says why: not pointed here, or another site on this server answers it). DELETE /v1/sites/<site>/domain (connector: remove_domain) disconnects it. A site with a domain lives only on that domain: its <site>.<handle>.simple-host.app URL answers 302 to https://<domain>/... (same path and query), writes through its other addresses answer 401 {"error":"this site saves on its own domain","code":"use_custom_domain","domain":"<domain>"} — key or not; agents write through the apex https://simple-host.app/v1/... as usual, and reads stay public — and /me there returns {"signed_in":false,"sign_in_available":false,"code":"use_custom_domain","domain":"<domain>"} so the page can link to the same page on the domain — SH.mount() renders that link and SH.requireSignIn() rejects with code use_custom_domain and .domain.
PRIVATE COLLECTIONS — for orders, RSVPs, survey answers, sign-ups, or anything with names, emails, phone numbers or addresses. Pages and public lists are readable by anyone; a private collection is readable only by the site owner (and the Simple Host operator, for moderation). A collection can be made private: only signed-in visitors can submit, and only you can read it. Any site can do this on its own address; no domain is needed. Steps: (1) PUT https://simple-host.app/v1/sites/<site>/collections/<coll>/privacy {"private":true} with X-API-Key (connector: set_collection_privacy) before the form goes live. {"private":false} makes everything already in it public (except _submitted_by: only the owner's reads include the submitters' emails), so confirm first. (2) The form page loads auth.js and does await SH.requireSignIn() then SH.collection('orders').append({...}); the item must be one JSON object; the server stamps _submitted_by (the visitor's verified email) and _submitted_at, and the 201 answer is the stored item, so show the visitor that. Only a visitor signed in on the site's own address can add; API keys and agents get 403 private_visitor_only; other addresses get 403 private_needs_own_domain; not signed in is 401 visitor_auth_required. (3) An owner admin page on the site (e.g. orders.html, linked quietly or not at all) does await SH.requireSignIn() then SH.collection('orders').list(); it works only when the owner's own account is signed in, and everyone else gets 404 not_found. Items carry an id: the owner can SH.collection('orders').update(id,{status:'done'}) (PATCH .../collections/<coll>/items/<id>; null removes a field; the stamps never change) and SH.collection('orders').remove(id) (DELETE; the item stays in the list's Recently deleted for 30 days). In a public list the owner can delete an item (spam; DELETE .../items/<id>) but not edit it (409 append_only), and the owner can empty any list with DELETE /v1/sites/<site>/collections/<coll> and {"confirm":"<coll>"} (connector: delete_collection_item, clear_collection). Visitors cannot read back, edit or delete their own items or anyone else's. The owner also reads it with X-API-Key (GET .../collections/<coll> adds "private":true), GET /v1/sites/<site>/collections (each entry has "private"), the CSV export and the dashboard.
UNDO AND WHO WROTE IT — every change to a site's state (PUT, PATCH) and every edit, delete or clear of a list item is kept for 30 days with who made it and when. Owner only (X-API-Key or connector): GET /v1/sites/<site>/state/history (newest first; ?limit, ?before=next), GET .../state/history/<id> (value = the document just before that change), POST .../state/history/<id>/restore (puts it back; a restore is itself undoable). Lists: GET /v1/sites/<site>/collections/<coll>/history, .../history/<id>, POST .../history/<id>/restore (a delete or clear brings the item back, an edit puts its fields back); GET .../collections/<coll>/deleted (Recently deleted), POST .../collections/<coll>/items/<id>/restore, POST .../collections/<coll>/deleted/restore {"all":true} (undo a clear). Connector: data_history, restore_data, list_deleted, restore_item. Clearing a list or deleting an item moves it to Recently deleted; after 30 days it is gone for good. To remove something for good sooner (a visitor asked to be erased; a spam flood): DELETE .../collections/<coll>/deleted/<id> (one item of Recently deleted, with its history), DELETE .../collections/<coll>/deleted {"confirm":"<coll>"} (all of it), DELETE /v1/sites/<site>/history {"confirm":"<site>"} (every earlier version of the site's saved data and lists; the data itself stays); connector: delete_forever, only after the person confirms exactly what. Every owner route above also has a /v1/u/<handle>/sites/<site>/... form. Recently deleted pages with ?before=<next> (an opaque cursor). Every item a signed-in visitor sends, public lists included, records who sent it: the owner's reads show "by" (CSV: sent_by); public reads and the POST answer never do. Retry a POST or PATCH that may have landed with the same Idempotency-Key header (any unique string per write): for a writer with an identity (the owner's key or connector, or a signed-in visitor) it is saved once and answered again (Idempotent-Replayed: true; an append with its item, a PATCH with the document as it is now); the same key with another body is 409 idempotency_key_reused; 409 idempotency_in_progress while the first is still running; writes made without signing in ignore the header. PATCH keeps numbers exact. Limits carry a code: 413 item_too_large, 429 rate_limited (saved-data reads: 30 a second per site and address, or per account with a key; list items added without the owner's key: 30 a minute per address), 507 site_full (the write would grow the site's live saved data, page data plus list items, past 50 MB; history and Recently deleted do not count, writes that do not grow it always go through, and deleting items or clearing a list makes room at once).
Write with plain fetch after the visitor signs in (below). Always send credentials:'include' and X-SH-CSRF: 1; the call is same-origin on the site's address, and the same code keeps working if a domain is connected later:
const m=location.hostname.startsWith('sites.')&&location.pathname.match(/^\/([^/]+)\/([^/]+)\//); const API=m?'/v1/u/'+m[1]+'/sites/'+m[2]:'/v1/sites/[YOUR-SITE-NAME]';
await fetch(API+'/state',{method:'PATCH',credentials:'include',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json','X-SH-CSRF':'1'},body:JSON.stringify({ops:[{op:'inc',path:'total',by:1}]})});
await fetch(API+'/collections/entries',{method:'POST',credentials:'include',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json','X-SH-CSRF':'1'},body:JSON.stringify(item)});
Read with GET API+'/state' and GET API+'/collections/entries?limit=50'. Check response.ok; a non-2xx is a failed save.
Any page that saves loads <script src="https://simple-host.app/auth.js" defer></script>, then SH.mount('#sh-auth') after DOMContentLoaded with a matching <section id="sh-auth"></section>, and awaits SH.requireSignIn() before each save. On <site>.<handle>.simple-host.app auth.js finds the site from the host name (on the <handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/ fallback, from the page path); window.SH_CONFIG={site:'your-site'} also works there and is what a custom domain needs. The API stays same-origin. SH.state.patch({ops:[...]}), SH.collection('entries').append(item), SH.state.get() and SH.collection('entries').list() do the fetches above for you, with the credentials and CSRF header included.
Sign-in is Google or an emailed code. SH.email.request(email) sends a 6-digit code; SH.email.verify(email,code) signs in. Visitor verification never returns an API key. SH.me() returns the server body: {"signed_in":true,...} or {"signed_in":false,...}.
Shared data belongs on the server, not in localStorage/sessionStorage. State and public lists are readable by anyone; do not store secrets in them. Keep forms visible on errors; never claim success on failure or repeat a successful append to retry a failed count update.
Agents write with the site owner's X-API-Key through the apex https://simple-host.app/v1/...; another account's key gets 404 site not found and writes nothing. Invalid keys return 401 invalid_api_key. Keep keys out of page HTML. WRITE_AUTH_MODE=log/off and the owner's allow_anonymous_writes override are compatibility exceptions.
If the page collects entries, include a matching admin.html that reads and renders them. For a public list it can be linked from index.html. For a private list it is the owner admin page above, which works only for the owner. Use a solid page background.

ANALYTICS — INFORMATIONAL, BUILD NOTHING FOR IT. Traffic is counted server-side from the access log: never add a hit counter, beacon, or analytics script to the page. Two read-only owner endpoints, X-API-Key, owner-scoped, days defaults to 30 (clamped 1..365):
GET /v1/sites/<name>/analytics?days=30 → {range_days, classified_from, totals, last_24h, daily:[{day,...}], hourly:[{hour,...}]}. daily is zero-filled dense over the window; hourly is always 24 buckets ending with the hour in progress.
GET /v1/analytics/sites?days=30 → {range_days, sites:[{name,...}]} — every site you own, ordered by person.views descending. Admins only may add &all=1 for every site on the box; anyone else gets 403.
PATCH /v1/sites/<name> with {"name":"new-name"} renames a site and moves its files. A custom domain stays attached. Links to the old address redirect to the new one (path and query kept) until a new site is created with the old name; use site_url from the response.
PATCH /v1/sites/<name> with {"offline":true} takes a site offline: every address shows a plain "This site is offline" page (503), and visitor saves (private lists too), visitors' reads of its saved data and lists, and visitor sign-in are refused (403 site_offline); files, versions and saved data are kept, and the owner's key still deploys, reads and writes. {"offline":false} puts it back online. GET /v1/sites marks such a site "offline": true.
API KEYS — each sign-in adds a key (starts shk_; older bare-hex keys keep working; stored only as hashes and never shown again). GET /v1/me/keys lists them (id, name, last4, created_at, last_used_at, current). POST /v1/me/keys {"name":"GitHub Actions"} mints a named key, shown once. DELETE /v1/me/keys/<id> revokes one. POST /v1/me/sign-out ends the key sent with it. POST /v1/me/api-key/rotate ("Sign out everywhere") returns a new api_key, invalidates every older key immediately and disconnects connected apps; update the agent or CLI with the new key. POST /v1/auth/verify takes an optional "name" for the key it issues. Owner-route 401s carry code missing_api_key, wrong_auth_header or invalid_api_key.
DELETE /v1/sites/<name> takes a site offline at once and keeps it, with every version and all its saved data, in Recently deleted for 7 days; its name stays taken until then (a POST with that name answers 409 with "recently_deleted": true). GET /v1/me/deleted-sites lists them with purge_at; POST /v1/sites/<name>/restore brings one back exactly as it was. After 7 days it is removed for good. Idle sites: on simple-host.app a site with no visitors, no new version and no saved data for 90 days gets its owner an email with a Keep it link (and a link to their page, where they can sign in and download it); 30 days later with nothing done it moves to Recently deleted (a second email has a Restore it link). Each link opens a page whose button does the action. Any restore restarts the clock. GET /v1/sites shows idle_removal_at on such a site. Sites with their own domain or name are never flagged; PUT /v1/sites/<name>/keep {"keep":true} (connector: keep_site) keeps any site up for good.
YOUR DATA — GET /v1/me/export.zip (the older /v1/me/export.tar.gz address serves the same zip; the person's own X-API-Key; a connected app gets 400 not_an_account_key; a suspended account gets 403 account_suspended and writes to support@simple-host.app for a copy) streams one .zip of everything held about the account: README.txt, account.json (email, handle, display name, created, old handles, claimed names, custom domains, linked sign-ins), keys.json (names, last 4, dates; never keys), connected_apps.json, visitor.json (sites signed in to as a visitor, every entry sent to other people's lists while signed in, and every change made to other people's page data while signed in: site, what, change, when) sites/<name>/ per live site (same layout as the per-site export) and recently-deleted/<name>/ per site in Recently deleted (same layout plus deleted.json with deleted_at and removed_for_good_at; collections.json entries are {id, created_at, submitted_by, data}; submitted_by is the address the visitor signed in with on that site). DELETE /v1/me {"confirm":"<handle>"} (the email when the account has no handle) deletes the account and ALL its data at once and for good — every site including Recently deleted ones, keys, connected apps, and the entries the person sent to other people's lists while signed in; their address is taken off the changes they made to other people's page data (writes made without signing in and older public-list entries are not linked to anyone and stay; support@simple-host.app helps with those); the handle and site names are retired, never reused. Only with the person's own key (a connected app gets 400 not_an_account_key); 400 confirm_mismatch, 403 account_suspended, site_suspended (a site the operator took down; the operator handles that account) or admin_account, 409 event_hostnames. Never call it unless the person explicitly asks to delete their account, and offer the download first. The person can also use "Your data" on their page.
SIGN-IN EMAIL AND ALERTS — POST /v1/me/email {"email":"new@example.com"} sends a 6-digit code to the new address and another to the current one (current_email); POST /v1/me/email/verify {"code":"123456","current_code":"654321"} needs both and moves the account there (the handle, sites and connected apps stay; every other key is signed out, the calling one stays; linked Google/GitHub sign-ins stay and are listed at GET /v1/me/identities, removable with DELETE /v1/me/identities/<id>; open codes for the old address stop; the old address gets a notice with a 7-day undo link). The person's own key only (400 not_an_account_key); 400 same_email, invalid_email, codes_required, no_pending_change, reserved_email; 401 invalid_code; 403 for the reviewer, admin, event and preview accounts; 409 email_taken (another account signs in with it, said only after the codes). After each sign-in (code, link, Google) or app connection the person gets one short email: time (UTC), browser or app, and a link to Sign out everywhere; at most one per browser a day; never for API key calls. GET /v1/me returns signin_alerts; PATCH /v1/me {"signin_alerts": false} turns them off (own key only). The person can do both under "Sign-in" on their page.
Every bucket (totals, last_24h, each daily, each hourly, each site) is the SAME four-class split — person, bot, infra, unknown — each {views, visitors}. There is NO top-level views or visitors.
person = no automation signature; READ THIS AS THE AUDIENCE NUMBER. bot = crawlers, AI scrapers, SEO tools, security scanners, HTTP libraries. infra = uptime probes and health checks, usually the biggest number and never audience. unknown = days recorded before traffic was classified; report it separately, never folded into the other three.
visitors = distinct hashed IPs over the window asked for, so totals.*.visitors is NOT the sum of the daily figures (one person on five days = 1 in totals, 5 in daily). Views count 200/304 GET document responses only, for every class alike.

SELF-CHECK before you publish: page writes use fetch with credentials:'include' and X-SH-CSRF: 1 (or SH.state/SH.collection); every page that saves loads auth.js and awaits SH.requireSignIn() before saving; links are relative (css/style.css, never /css/...); shared data uses state/collections; API keys never appear in page code; failed writes keep the form visible; successful appends are never repeated; collected entries have an organizer view; personal details go only into a private collection on the site's own address; the background is solid.

PUBLISHING — without the connector, this is how the site goes live. Pick a short lowercase name (letters, digits, hyphens). Create it once with POST, change it afterwards with PUT:
  POST https://simple-host.app/v1/sites/<name>/files   with header X-API-Key: <key>, body {"files":{"index.html":"<the page>"}}
  PUT  https://simple-host.app/v1/sites/<name>/files   same body, for every later change
A 409 on POST means that name is already yours: use PUT. Binary files go in files_base64 instead, base64-encoded. The response carries site_url (https://<name>.<handle>.simple-host.app/, or briefly https://<handle>.simple-host.app/<name>/ for a new account), which is the link to share. Every deploy is versioned; GET /v1/sites/<name>/versions lists the versions this instance still holds and PUT /v1/sites/<name>/active-version switches to one of them. To look before it goes live, PUT with ?publish=false: the version is stored, not made live (status "ready" in the list), and the answer carries unpublished_version and preview_url, a link that works for anyone who has it, for one hour (give it only to the person) (POST /v1/sites/<name>/versions/<n>/preview-link mints one for any kept version; connector: update_site publish false, preview_version). Pages opened from a preview cannot save (403 preview_read_only). Make it live with active-version. An event instance may keep only the live version to save disk, in which case that list has one entry and redeploying is how you go back. Take a copy any time with GET /v1/sites/<name>/export.tar.gz (files, state.json, collections.json). With no key to send (the connector), POST /v1/sites/<name>/export-link (connector: export_site) returns a download link that works for 10 minutes; give it to the person, never post it publicly.
Errors are JSON {"error":"...","code":"..."}; branch on code, not the wording: site_exists (409, that name is already yours: use PUT), domain_taken (409, the address belongs to someone else: pick another), invalid_name / name_reserved (400, pick another name), invalid_domain (400), domain_releasing (409, that domain was just disconnected: try again in 10 minutes), rate_limited (429, wait and retry), site_quota_reached (403), append_only (409, public list items cannot be changed), custom_domain_required (409, give the site its own address first), missing_api_key / invalid_api_key (401), site_suspended (403, the operator has taken the site down: changes are refused until it is restored; tell the person, do not retry), account_suspended (403, the operator has suspended this account; tell the person), site_offline (403, the owner took the site offline: visitors cannot save, read its data or sign in until it is back online; the owner's key still reads and writes).
Read a retained version (owner API key): GET /v1/sites/<name>/versions/<n>/files lists paths and byte sizes; GET /v1/sites/<name>/versions/<n>/files/<path> returns raw file bytes with sandbox CSP. Pruned versions return 404.

AGENT SAVING — POST /v1/auth {"email":"person@example.com"}, then POST /v1/auth/verify with that email and the person's emailed code to receive api_key. Send X-API-Key on state/collections writes through the apex; a key writes only sites its own account owns (another account's key gets 404). A private collection is the exception: only signed-in visitors on the site's own address add to it; the owner's key reads, edits and deletes its items.

CONNECTOR — chat apps (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok) add https://simple-host.app/mcp as a remote MCP connector. It uses OAuth 2.1 (discovery at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp, dynamic registration, PKCE S256): the person signs in once in a browser window and every later chat is signed in. Its tools (create_site, update_site, list_sites, get_site, read_site_file, rollback_site, delete_site, get_state, update_state, list_collections, read_collection, add_to_collection, connect_domain, domain_status, remove_domain, set_collection_privacy, update_collection_item, delete_collection_item, clear_collection, data_history, restore_data, list_deleted, restore_item, delete_forever, …) call this same API as that person. An access token issued without a resource (a GPT Action) is also accepted as Authorization: Bearer on /v1 with exactly the person's API-key permissions. GET /v1/me/connections lists connected apps; DELETE /v1/me/connections/<client_id> disconnects one.

Event instances: admins can POST /v1/admin/users with {"emails":["a@example.com"]} or {"count":30,"prefix":"team"} to issue participant keys without sign-in. There is no limit on how many. GET /v1/admin/usage reports what the disk is actually holding, what is free, and warns as it fills; it also names the running release (version, commit) and the per-site cap and deploys kept in force (site_limit_mb, keep_versions).  DELETE /v1/admin/users/{id} removes a non-admin account and all its data, the same erasure as DELETE /v1/me. Take-down without deleting: POST /v1/admin/sites/{id}/suspend {"reason":"..."} (every address shows "This site has been taken down", changes refused) and .../restore; POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/suspend {"reason":"..."} (keys, connected apps and sign-in refused, all their sites down) and .../enable. GET /v1/admin/export.tar.gz downloads every site with its saved data and lists as one archive. GET /v1/admin/data-watch counts, per site, the saved-data uses a later step tightens (visitor whole-document replace, non-object documents, visitor ops by type, large visitor inc, new list names, large items). GET /v1/admin/idle-sites is the idle-site cleanup's dry run (sites a run would warn or move to Recently deleted; the cleanup itself runs only with IDLE_CLEANUP=on). PATCH /v1/me edits display_name (trimmed, max 100 characters) or handle: freely before anything is published, then once every 30 days (429 with next_change_after otherwise); the old handle stays reserved for the account and every old address redirects to the new one, while what pages kept in visitors' browsers starts empty and visitors sign in again. GET /v1/auth/oauth/providers includes email_enabled as well as configured OAuth providers.
